"CONC PIUP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.qpv.ph DILG OPINION No. 22 s. 2024 FEB MR. EMMANUEL L. ESCRIBIR Municipal Assessor Many.escribir@yahoo.com Dear Mr. Escribir: This refers to your electronic mail dated June 27, 2023 requesting this Department's legal opinion relative to the appointment of the head of OSCA [Office of the Senior Citizen Affairs). As aptly cited, pursuant to Section 6 of Republic Act (RA) No. 9994, otherwise known as the "Expanded Senior Citizen Act of 2010", the head of the OSCA shall be appointed by the Mayor from a list of three (3) nominees selected by the general assembly. From the abovecited provision arose your query: If one of the nominees is a relative of the mayor within the fourth (4th) civil degree of consanguinity or affinity and he/she is appointed as the OSCA Head, is this not violative of Section 4(c) of RA 6713, which provides that: "Section 4. Norms of Conduct Of Public Officials and Employees. - (A) Every public official and employee shall observe the following as standards of personal conduct in the discharge and execution of official duties: (c) Justness and sincerity. - Public officials and employees shall remain true to the people at all times. They must act with justness and sincerity and shall not discriminate against anyone, especially the poor and the underprivileged. They shall at all times respect the rights of others, and shall refrain from doing acts contrary to law, good morals, good customs, public policy, public order, public safety and public interest. They shall not dispense or extend undue favors on account of their office to their relatives whether bv consanguinity or pffinity except with respect to appointments of such relatives to positions nsidered strictl confide tial or as me be their rsona sta whose term* are coterminous with theirs." This Department opines in the negative. For purposes Of discussion, it is to be noted that the afore-quoted provision is generally applicable to all public officials. Appointing others to positions by reason of blood or marital relationships to the appointing authority is nepotism and is prohibited by law. However, such relatives may be appointed if the position is strictly confidential or members of the personal staff of the appointing authority whose terms are coterminous with the latter. "Matlno, Mahusay at Maasahani' Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Nevertheless, insofar as appointment to local government positions is concerned, Section 79 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 (hereinafter referred to as the Code), finds application, thus: "Section 79. Limitation to Appointments. - No person shall be appointed in the career service of the local government if he is related within the fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity to the appointing or recommending authority." As can be gathered from the aforequoted provision, the prohibition on the appointment of a person who is related within the fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity to the appointing authority—in this case, the Municipal Mayor—applies only to positions in the career service. This now warrants a determination of whether the position of OSCA Head is considered a career service and, therefore, such a prohibition should be applicable. This may be answered by distinguishing career service from non-career service. Under the Administrative Code of 1987, Career Service is characterized by (I) entrance based on merit and fitness to be determined as far as practicable by competitive examination, or based on highly technical qualifications; (2) opportunity for advancement to higher career positions; and (3) security of tenure. On the other hand, Non-Career Service is characterized by (I) entrance on bases other than those of the usual tests of merit and fitness utilized for the career service; and (2) tenure, which is limited to a period specified by law, or which is coterminous with that of the appointing authority or subject to his pleasure, or which is limited to the durations of particular project for which purpose employment was made. Accordingly, the position of OSCA Head falls under the non-career position, specifically, the tenure is limited to a period specified by law. Section 6 of RA 9994 provides that the OSCA shall be headed by a senior citizen "who shall be appointed by the mayor for a term of three (3) years without reappointment but without prejudice to an extension if exigency so requires. Said appointee shall be chosen from a list of three (3) nominees as recommended by a general assembly of senior citizens organizations in the city or municipality. As such, the limitation on appointment set forth by the Code— as above-cited—is not applicable. Along this line, it is to be noted that appointments should not be conceived as 'favors'. The appointing authority is expected to exercise his discretion based on fair and just decisions. Verily, although the Code provides local chief executives with wide latitude of discretion as to who shall be appointed to a particular position, there are parameters put in place that need to be complied with to ensure effective governance and ultimately avoid concerns about nepotism and corruption, which can undermine the integrity of the government and its commitment to serve the public interest. Premised from the foregoing, this Department opines that for as long as the appointee possesses all the qualifications and none of the disqualifications provided by law and that pertinent laws have been duly complied with, then such appointment is proper. Page 2 of 3

This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you Very truly yours, By the Authority of the Secretary: ATTY. J Unders OUSEL OR R. LLAMAS ry for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs Page 3 of 3
